summary: Nothing further to add this cycle; the draft bytes are the correction landed last cycle (the snapshot-trigger Fact now at revision 2 with changed_premise 1f6e894a67e24249ab6b8dbbcd9e76e3-knowledge-0@1), so no duplicate revision is created. Final state of this run's record, for the independent reviewer: one asserted defect - shouldSnapshot compares the log store's last index against the cached snapshot index as unsigned values, so a node whose store sits below its snapshot index reports that it should snapshot even though applied and commit indices already equal the snapshot, witnessed twice over the production snapshot path (CheckRun 9cba2e79ff6c4019b0f0381690d9aaab: control false, emptied store true with commit/applied still 4) and by a follower installing a snapshot at an index above its own log store (CheckRun e5116cfe896549deb27799d6d871ed77: snapshot_index=8, store_last=5, true), with the consequence measured as redundant snapshot creation at the unchanged index (CheckRun a4a0cbfa094b4d1982032d9de0652861) and bounded to wasted snapshot work with no safety effect. Three suspicions were refuted with retained operands (non-voter acknowledgement cannot advance commitIndex; a restart preserves the durable last vote so no second different vote in a term; the AddVoter configuration lag was a bounded replication transient, with the user-restore and non-quiescent install routes also measured not to produce the snapshot condition). Four durable Behaviors/Facts cover the leader's append-time configuration and commitment updates, the follower's latest-configuration-at-store-time, the voter-only commit set, the durable last-vote read, and both snapshot-trigger mechanisms; the only unmeasured aspect left is the cadence of the redundant snapshot attempts, which needs an attempt-level observation rather than stored-snapshot counts.
